LanguageData.CBF_Lo_NewTip0: Create a new object list. You pick its structures.
LanguageData.CBF_Lo_NewTip1: Create a new, empty loot table. It reaches the file only when you save.
LanguageData.CBF_Lo_NewTip2: Create a new container, with images for full and empty.
LanguageData.CBF_Lo_PickOne: Pick an entry on the left.
LanguageData.CBF_Lo_OpenFileTip: Opens the file in your text editor. The editor reloads changes made there on its own.
LanguageData.CBF_Lo_ListHintTables: Red means: nothing in the table exists in the game.
LanguageData.CBF_Lo_NoParents: No other table draws this one.
LanguageData.CBF_Lo_FallbackTip: If this table yields nothing, the one picked here is drawn instead.
LanguageData.CBF_Lo_FileOnly: Only editable in the file, kept when saving: {0}
LanguageData.CBF_Lo_DisplayTip: Fill: containers are filled with loot. Empty: they are just furniture.
LanguageData.CBF_Lo_PawnInsideHint: With a pawn list someone can jump out when it is opened.
LanguageData.CBF_Lo_EditContainerTip: Opens the container window with this one as the template.
LanguageData.CBF_Lo_FooterHint: Changes reach the file only when you save.
LanguageData.CBF_Lo_SampleTip: Draws the saved table a few times and shows the result.
LanguageData.CBF_Lo_NewTip3: Create a new crop list. It reaches the file only when you save.
LanguageData.CBF_Lo_CropHint: Fields and pens that name this list draw their plants from it by weight. A change here affects all of them.
LanguageData.CBF_Lo_CropEmpty: No plants in the list yet.
LanguageData.CBF_Lo_CropUnused: No field and no pen names this list.
LanguageData.CBF_Lo_CropRightHint: In the Settlement tab you pick the list for each field and pen. Without a list, the individually chosen plants apply there.
LanguageData.CBF_Lo_CropNoProject: The mod folder was not found.
LanguageData.CBF_Lo_NewTip4: Create a new material list. It inherits from the base list and reaches the file only when you save.
LanguageData.CBF_Mat_MapStoneTip: Blocks from the rock of the map tile.
LanguageData.CBF_Mat_FloorMixTip: These floors are mixed by weight. You change the weights in the file.
LanguageData.CBF_Mat_TagSearchTip: When no entry of the chains exists, CBF looks for a thing or floor with this tag.
LanguageData.CBF_Mat_Missing: {0} is not loaded. The next entry is tried.
LanguageData.CBF_Mat_CriticalTip: Critical: if this role finds nothing, the whole list is unusable. Optional: the role simply stays empty.
LanguageData.CBF_Mat_WardTip: Limits this row to one kind of ward. A row for the ward wins over a row without one. It affects everything resolved by role in that ward: walls, roads and floors the generator draws, and cells of pieces that name a role instead of a concrete thing. Pieces that name concrete things keep them.
LanguageData.CBF_Mat_Hint: Pieces name roles instead of things. This list says what fills each role. The first existing entry of a chain wins. A role may appear in several rows, then the row that fits the piece or ward best is used.
LanguageData.CBF_Mat_Empty: No roles of its own yet.
LanguageData.CBF_Mat_OverrideTip: Copies the inherited rows into this list, so you can change them.
LanguageData.CBF_Mat_Unused: No settlement type names this list.
LanguageData.CBF_Mat_ParentTip: Roles this list does not name itself come from this list.
LanguageData.CBF_Mat_RightHint: In the Settlement tab every settlement type picks its material list. Previews of single pieces use the list of the settlement type selected there.
LanguageData.CBF_RoleTip_WALL: Outer walls of buildings and the settlement wall.
LanguageData.CBF_RoleTip_DOOR: Doors of buildings and doors in the wall, on the walkway, in towers and posterns.
LanguageData.CBF_RoleTip_GATE: Gate in a wall passage without a gatehouse.
LanguageData.CBF_RoleTip_EMBRASURE: Arrow slits and embrasures in walls and towers.
LanguageData.CBF_RoleTip_FLOOR_FINE: Floor for fine rooms such as halls and temples.
LanguageData.CBF_RoleTip_FLOOR_ROUGH: Floor for simple rooms such as barns and workshops.
LanguageData.CBF_RoleTip_FLOOR_ROAD: Roads, when the ward names no roads of its own.
LanguageData.CBF_RoleTip_FLOOR_ROAD_EDGE: Strip along the edge of the roads.
LanguageData.CBF_RoleTip_ROOF_THIN: Thin roof, for sheds and open halls.
LanguageData.CBF_RoleTip_CONTAINER: Crates and other containers for loot.
LanguageData.CBF_RoleTip_PEN_MARKER: Marker that turns a fenced area into an animal pen.
LanguageData.CBF_RoleTip_CONDUIT_ROAD: Conduit where it runs under roads.
LanguageData.CBF_Mat_AppliesToTip: Fortification pieces or categories this row is meant for, for example palisade walls. The row applies in wards whose walls, emplacements or gatehouses use one of them. Like Ward, it only affects what is resolved by role; pieces that name concrete things keep them.
LanguageData.CBF_Lo_FloorHint: Floor symbols of pieces that name this list draw their floor from it by weight. A change here affects all of them.
LanguageData.CBF_Lo_FloorFromMapTip: The floor is swapped for the variant made of the stone found on the map, as with floors without a list.
LanguageData.CBF_Lo_FloorMaterials: Materials, one is picked at random:
LanguageData.CBF_Lo_FloorMaterialsTip: Only the ticked materials are used. With none ticked, exactly this floor is laid, without swapping for the map's stone.
LanguageData.CBF_Lo_FloorUnused: No piece names this list yet.
LanguageData.CBF_Lo_FloorRightHint: In the Piece tab you pick the list for each floor symbol under Floors. Without a list, the floor drawn in the piece is laid.
